pure-announcement.rationale: It introduces a development methodology — spec-first backlogs, acceptance-criteria contracts, staged delivery waves, governance from day one — rather than announcing a product; the template repo is illustrative material, not the point.

duplicate.rationale: The supplied nearest concepts are MCP-platform and skills-format notes; none covers applying Agile process discipline to human-agent development teams.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The claims rest on a public template repo and a described project history (Minthe), and the central mechanism — process gates and locked specs reduce agent drift — is something a reader can apply and check.

durability.rationale: Its core argument — agent failures at scale are process problems fixed by specs, contract acceptance criteria and early governance, not by better models — is a pattern that outlives the named tools (Copilot CLI, GPT-5.5, CLAUDE.md).

actionability.rationale: It prescribes adoptable practices with rationale: every capability becomes an issue with acceptance criteria and file-ownership tables, CI is the first story rather than the last, review gates sit between waves, and retrospectives feed the process back.

atomicity.rationale: The practices are facets of one stateable idea — run human-agent development as contract-driven Agile — not a bundle of unrelated claims.
